deals.debtNotes: Not part of the assumable Guggenheim loan pool. The $100,441,000 / 5.25% / Nov-2032 assumable financing encumbers a nine-asset subset (Brickyard Plaza, Fairview Commons, Gold Star Plaza, Golden Triangle, Hamburg Square, Pine Grove Plaza, Southington Center, Trexler Mall, Washington Center Shoppes) - Sunshine Shopping Plaza is unencumbered.
deals.proximityHighways: Straight-line configuration at the high-traffic intersection of Homestead Road North and South Loop Boulevard (26,000 VPD) in Lehigh Acres, east of Fort Myers.
deals.retailCotenants: Homestead Shopping Plaza sits adjacent. Nearby demand drivers include Veterans Park, Lehigh Acres Park North and an expanded Lee County park and athletic complex. Substantial residential construction is underway within the trade area: Ibis Landing Golf & Country Club by Lennar (980 homes under construction), Savanna Lakes by Lennar (630 planned), Bentley Crossing by D.R. Horton (283 under construction), Whispering Lakes by Centex (290 planned) and by M/I Homes (145 planned), and Avalon (148 under construction).

marketDemographics.source: Project Evergreen property OM (CBRE), Demographics page - 2025 current-year estimates
marketDemographics.note: The fastest-growing trade area in Project Evergreen by a wide margin. 3-mile population is up 57% since 2010 (35,428 to 55,766) and growing 2.91% annually from 2020 to 2025, with a further 1.98% annually projected through 2030; 5-mile population is growing 3.05% annually. Average household income is projected to rise roughly 19% by 2030 across every ring. The OM also publishes a True Trade Area of 85,981 population at $88,454 average household income, and notes the 3-mile trade area is conservatively estimated to be 50% Hispanic. Note the OM's daytime population figures are unusually low relative to residential population, consistent with a bedroom community east of Fort Myers.

deals.notes: Sunshine Shopping Plaza is a 111,189 SF, 100%-leased neighborhood center on approximately 11.4 acres at the signalized intersection of Homestead Road North and South Loop Boulevard (26,000 VPD) in Lehigh Acres, Florida, built between 1966 and 1980. Fresco y Mas anchors 47,922 SF, 43% of the GLA, and is the reason to own this asset: 2025 sales of $36,526,117, or $762 PSF, against base rent of $6.00 PSF and subsidized recoveries produce a 1.03% occupancy cost - among the healthiest grocery positions imaginable and the only full-size Hispanic grocer serving the Fort Myers market, in a 3-mile trade area the OM estimates is 50% Hispanic. Ace Hardware (13,500 SF, $576 PSF, 2.96% occupancy cost, top 2% of its Florida chain by foot traffic per Placer.ai) and Family Dollar (10,200 SF, $293 PSF, 4.72%) round out a genuinely productive roster averaging $600 PSF at a 1.89% blended health ratio. In-place base rent from the 9/1/2026 rent roll is $1,211,495, or $10.90 PSF against CBRE's market, and in-place NOI is $1,083,343 on $1,587,092 of effective gross revenue. The trade area is the growth story of the portfolio: 3-mile population is up 57% since 2010 and still compounding at 2.91% annually, with roughly 2,300 homes under construction or planned within the trade area by Lennar, D.R. Horton, Centex and M/I Homes, and household income projected up 19% by 2030. The nuance a buyer has to hold in mind is that Fresco y Mas's $6.00 PSF is LOCKED - three five-year options at a flat $6.00 carry it to June 2045 - so 43% of the building generates rent that cannot be reset for nineteen years. That is exceptionally secure income, not upside, and it is why the in-place rent looks 41% below market. What genuinely grows is the 1% percentage rent over a natural breakpoint, which CBRE projects rising from $29,740 to $134,465 over the hold as sales compound, plus the rollover of essentially the entire non-grocery roster during a ten-year hold. Two data points deserve scrutiny before the growth case is accepted: Made For This Fitness reports a 37.7% occupancy cost, and Leslie's Pool a 10.8%, both well above sustainable thresholds.
keyAssumptions: SOURCES: roster built from the WHLR MRI rent roll dated 9/1/2026 (authoritative for current tenant, suite, SF, rent, dates and contractual steps); options, recovery methods, reported sales, occupancy-cost health ratios and percentage-rent terms from the CBRE Argus model Project Evergreen_FL_Sunshine Shopping Plaza (FINAL).xlsx dated 8/21/2026; historical income and expense from the WHLR income statement for the 12 months ended December 2025 (entity WHLRSU); assessed value and tax detail from the Argus assumptions page; demographics, traffic count, parking count, Placer.ai chain rankings and property description from the property OM.

ROSTER TIE-OUT: 22 leases sum to 111,189 SF, exactly the rent roll's stated GLA (0 SF vacant, 100.0% occupied). Monthly base rent sums to $100,957.89, exactly the roll's printed total; annualized = $1,211,495.

HEADLINE NOI BASIS: noi / effectiveGrossIncome / operatingExpenses are CBRE's published In-Place Pro-Forma for calendar 2027 ($1,587,092 EGR less $503,749 of operating expense = $1,083,343), which ties exactly and is the basis behind the OM's stated in-place NOI. The VDR portfolio table rounds this to $1,080,000. EGR includes $29,740 of Fresco y Mas percentage rent.

RECOVERIES BASIS: nnnRecoveries of $338,365 and the per-tenant expenseReimbursements are CBRE's in-place figures and combine BOTH the operating-expense recovery ($186,994) and the separately-stated real estate tax recovery ($151,369). CBRE's published total is $338,363; the per-tenant table sums to $338,365, a $2 rounding difference. The rent roll's monthly cost-recovery column totals $327,597 annualized - close, because Florida taxes are billed within the monthly recovery here.

GPR RECONCILIATION: grossPotentialRent of $1,211,495 is the 9/1/2026 roll's in-place base rent and ties to the roster. CBRE's in-place pro-forma base rent of $1,218,989 is $7,494 higher because it runs contractual steps landing during calendar 2027.

THE OM SITE PLAN SHOWS BLENDED, NOT CONTRACT, RENT: several rents on the OM site plan differ from the rent roll because CBRE presents a calendar-2027 blended figure. A1 Pharmacy shows $16.07 on the site plan against a $20.50 contract rent (the lease expires 3/31/2027); Country Style Ice Cream shows $15.36 against $18.00 (expires 5/31/2027). The roster carries CONTRACT rent from the rent roll throughout.

ACTUAL vs IN-PLACE: the owner's YE-2025 income statement shows actual NOI of $1,004,169 on $1,506,158 of total income and $501,989 of operating expense. The gap to CBRE's $1,083,343 in-place figure is mostly revenue: 2025 base rent of $1,103,912 predates several 2026 lease commencements and step-ups (Rent-A-Center, China Star, Made For This Fitness and UNIV 2 Liquor all commenced or renewed in 2025-2026), and 2025 recoveries were reduced by roughly $20,252 of negative prior-year true-ups. Expense loads are closely comparable ($501,989 actual versus $503,749 modeled).

TAXES: the Argus assumptions page discloses a 2025 assessed value of $13,180,680, 2025 ad valorem taxes of $156,831 and non-ad-valorem assessments of $11,445 - together $168,276, which ties exactly to the YE-2025 income statement's Real Estate Tax Expense of $168,275.86. CBRE explicitly did NOT reassess and modeled taxes at 2026 budgeted amounts. Florida reassesses to market on a change of ownership for non-homestead commercial property, so a sale at a basis materially above $13.2 million will step taxes up - this is a live underwriting item that CBRE has left to the buyer. CBRE also did NOT adjust insurance, modeling 2026 budgeted property insurance at $0.45 PSF and liability at $0.22 PSF; Florida coastal insurance should be re-underwritten to a buyer's own program.

SALES BASIS: salesPSF and occupancyCost are CBRE's In-Place Pro-Forma reported sales and health ratios. Fresco y Mas's $36,526,117 is a stated 2025 figure. Only six tenants report sales; the rest are null rather than estimated. Upload the sales report through the app's sales-report import to build the full trend history.

CHINA STAR AND FIESTA INSURANCE - RENEWALS IN PROCESS: CBRE notes China Star's lease currently expires 8/31/2026 with a 5-year renewal amendment IN PROCESS at $24.00 PSF with 3% annual increases, and Fiesta Insurance's lease currently expires 11/30/2026 with a 3-year renewal amendment IN PROCESS at $19.99 PSF. The 9/1/2026 rent roll already shows China Star on a new term running 9/1/2026 to 8/31/2031, so that one appears executed; Fiesta's roll expiry is still 11/30/2026, so its renewal is NOT yet reflected. Confirm execution of both. Fiesta is only 1,000 SF and $17,389 of rent, so the exposure is small, but leaseExpiry carries the roll's 11/30/2026 date rather than CBRE's assumed 11/30/2029.

NEW LEASES ON THE ROLL: the rent roll's New Leases section carries follow-on terms for Domino's (6/1/2028-5/31/2033), NDV Enterprises / Shipping Station (8/1/2027-7/31/2032) and Mariokan Academy (10/1/2026-9/30/2029). leaseExpiry reflects those committed terms; current contract rent is held so base rent ties to the roll.

LEASE CLAUSES ARE OM-SOURCED, NOT ABSTRACTED: the recovery structures, CAM caps and percentage-rent terms recorded in tenant notes come from CBRE's Argus lease summaries, not from executed lease documents. They are unverified and should be confirmed against the leases in diligence.
NO PRICING: the portfolio is marketed unpriced, so askingPrice, capRate and pricePerSF are null rather than estimated.

redFlags.description: Fresco y Mas is 43% of GLA at a rent that cannot be reset for nineteen years. Base rent is $6.00 PSF flat, with THREE five-year options at a flat $6.00 carrying the tenant to June 2045, and CAM and insurance FIXED at $11,980.50 per year with no growth (tenant pays pro rata real estate taxes only over a $57,409.37 base year). A tenant at a 1.03% occupancy cost on $762 PSF sales will never leave, so this is the most secure income in the portfolio - but 43% of the building generates rent that neither grows nor can be marked to market, its recovery contribution is frozen in nominal dollars while expenses inflate at 3%, and that combination caps both income growth and exit value. Underwrite it as a bond, not as embedded upside.

Made For This Fitness reports a 37.7% occupancy cost - 2,653 SF at $12.00 PSF with reported sales of roughly $39 PSF against $38,811 of total tenant revenue. Even allowing that gym membership revenue is not directly comparable to retail sales PSF, a ratio near 38% is not a viable operating position. The lease expires 2/28/2029 with no renewal options. Treat this as re-leasing exposure, and ask what the reported figure actually captures.

Leslie's Pool occupancy cost of 10.8% - 3,400 SF at $17.60 PSF on reported sales of $202 PSF. High for a specialty hard-goods retailer, and Leslie's has been closing underperforming stores nationally. The lease expires 12/31/2028 with two options at $19.36 and $21.30 PSF; at a 10.8% ratio today, an option exercise at a 10% higher rent should not be assumed. 3,400 SF of exposure.

Florida reassessment on sale is unmodeled and material. The 2025 assessed value is $13,180,680 against $168,276 of total taxes. CBRE explicitly states taxes have NOT been reassessed and are held at 2026 budgeted amounts, leaving the reassessment to the investor. Florida non-homestead commercial property resets to just value on a qualifying change of ownership, so a purchase materially above the current assessment flows straight into NOI. Separately, CBRE did NOT adjust insurance, holding 2026 budget at $0.45 PSF property and $0.22 PSF liability - Florida windstorm exposure means a buyer's actual program could differ substantially.

Nearly the entire non-grocery roster rolls during a ten-year hold, which is the growth case and the risk case at once. CBRE shows cumulative lease expirations reaching 83.8% of GLA by 2030 and 100% by 2035, with Fresco y Mas the only long-term position. That is what drives the projected 69% NOI growth, but it also means the income is being re-underwritten almost entirely over the hold - in a trade area where average household income is only $85,504 at three miles and $60,314 at one mile.

Concentrated near-term small-shop rollover with no options. A1 Pharmacy (1,700 SF, expires 3/31/2027), Country Style Ice Cream (1,400 SF, 5/31/2027), Direct General Insurance (2,450 SF, 3/31/2028), Final Touch Salon (1,000 SF, 8/31/2028) and Tyler Triplett Real Estate (446 SF, 6/30/2028) all expire within two years of a 2027 closing with NO renewal options recorded. Family Dollar (10,200 SF, 9.2% of GLA) expires 12/31/2027 with a single option at $10.80 PSF - CBRE assumes exercise.

Fiesta Insurance's renewal is not executed on the rent roll. CBRE models the lease to 11/30/2029 based on a 3-year renewal amendment described as in process at $19.99 PSF, but the 9/1/2026 rent roll still shows expiry 11/30/2026. Small exposure (1,000 SF, $17,389) but it is a modeled rather than contracted term - confirm execution.

Older improvements - the center was built between 1966 and 1980, making it the oldest asset in Project Evergreen. The YE-2025 statement shows only $24,115 of repairs and maintenance and $19,754 of structural and roof spend against $61,154 of security expense, which is itself notable: security is the second-largest controllable line at the center. Order a property condition assessment and understand why security costs run this high.

A thin one-mile income ring - $60,314 average household income within one mile against $85,504 at three miles and $88,694 at five. The immediate ring is materially poorer than the trade area, which supports the value-oriented merchandising (Fresco y Mas, Family Dollar, Rent-A-Center, Advance America) but limits how far shop rents can be pushed on rollover.

upsideItems.item: An exceptional grocery anchor in a rapidly growing, underserved trade area
upsideItems.detail: Fresco y Mas does $36,526,117 in annual sales, or $762 PSF, at a 1.03% occupancy cost, and is the ONLY full-size Hispanic grocer serving the Fort Myers market against a 3-mile trade area estimated at 50% Hispanic. Placer.ai ranks it in the top 13% of Florida chain foot traffic, with Ace Hardware in the top 2% and Family Dollar in the top 23%. Sales productivity at that level with rent at 1% of sales is about as durable as grocery income gets, and it anchors traffic for the entire shop line.

upsideItems.item: Percentage rent that grows with the grocer even though base rent cannot
upsideItems.detail: Fresco y Mas pays 1% of gross sales over a natural breakpoint, offset by expense reimbursements. CBRE projects that participation rising from $29,740 in 2027 to $134,465 by 2037 - a 352% increase - as sales compound. This is the one mechanism by which ownership participates in the anchor's growth while base rent stays locked at $6.00, and it is real, contractual and already being paid.

upsideItems.item: The fastest-growing trade area in the portfolio, with visible new supply of rooftops
upsideItems.detail: 3-mile population is up 57% since 2010 and compounding at 2.91% annually, with 5-mile at 3.05%. Roughly 2,300 homes are under construction or planned within the trade area - Ibis Landing by Lennar (980 under construction), Savanna Lakes by Lennar (630 planned), Bentley Crossing by D.R. Horton (283 under construction), Whispering Lakes by Centex (290) and M/I Homes (145), and Avalon (148). Average household income is projected up roughly 19% by 2030 in every ring. Under the demographics-to-rent lens, rising population AND rising income together is the strongest combination in Project Evergreen and directly supports the rollover mark-to-market case.

upsideItems.item: Genuine, capturable mark-to-market on the shop line
upsideItems.detail: Unlike the anchor, the shops roll with short or no option chains and sit meaningfully below CBRE's $14.00-$26.00 PSF shop market rents: A1 Pharmacy $20.50 vs $24.00, Direct General $17.22 vs $24.00, Advance America $13.33 vs $26.00, Country Style Ice Cream $18.00 vs $24.00, Final Touch $18.00 vs $24.00, Made For This Fitness $12.00 vs $14.00. With cumulative expirations reaching 83.8% of GLA by 2030, this is where CBRE's projected 69% NOI growth and 5.4% ten-year CAGR actually come from, and the tenants rolling are small enough that individual failures do not threaten the center.

upsideItems.item: Contractual step-ups already in place across the shop roster
upsideItems.detail: Eleven leases carry contracted increases landing between October 2026 and July 2030 - Magic Nails, Asian Buffet (five annual steps), A&A Salon, Advance America, Domino's, CubaMax, China Star (four annual steps), Final Touch, Shipping Station, Mariokan and UNIV 2 Liquor (stepping from $19.00 to $22.50 in July 2030). Growth arrives without leasing risk on this portion of the roll.

upsideItems.item: Fully leased with no vacancy carry and no debt to assume or refinance
upsideItems.detail: All 111,189 SF is leased as of 9/1/2026, so there is no lease-up cost in going-in NOI and CBRE still projects 97-99% physical occupancy across the hold. The asset is also unencumbered - it is not in the nine-property Guggenheim pool - so it can be financed or sold independently without release-payment mechanics or a $26.87 million pool release cap.

tenants.rentSchedule: Flat at $6.00 PSF ($23,961.00/month) through 6/30/2030 - no contractual increases in the current term.
tenants.renewalOptions: Three 5-year options at a FLAT $6.00 PSF: 7/2030-6/2035, 7/2035-6/2040 and 7/2040-6/2045. No rent increase at any option.
tenants.rentBumps: None - base rent is flat at $6.00 PSF through June 2045 if all options are exercised. The only growth is percentage rent.
tenants.assumptionNote: The anchor and the reason to own the asset. 43.1% of GLA. CBRE shows original occupancy May 1989 - roughly 37 years of continuous grocery operation at the site. 2025 sales of $36,526,117 ($762 PSF) at a 1.03% occupancy cost is exceptional; Placer.ai ranks the store in the top 13% of its Florida chain by foot traffic, and it is the only full-size Hispanic grocer serving the Fort Myers market against a 3-mile trade area estimated at 50% Hispanic. RECOVERY STRUCTURE IS THE CATCH: CAM and insurance are FIXED at $11,980.50 per year with no growth, so the anchor's contribution to controllable expenses erodes in real terms every year while the center's costs inflate at 3%. Tenant pays pro rata real estate taxes only over a $57,409.37 base year. PERCENTAGE RENT: 1% of gross sales over a natural breakpoint, offset by expense reimbursements - $29,740 in CY2027 rising to $134,465 by 2037 on CBRE's projection. Base rent of $6.00 is 60% below CBRE's $15.00 PSF anchor market rent, but with flat options to June 2045 that gap is permanently locked - secure, bond-like income that caps growth and exit value, never capturable upside.
